label: FIXTURE RESULT: pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation
symptom: Customers say that transfer notifications are arriving late.

report.summary: Outbox backlog built up (pending up to 125, oldest undelivered age up to 38.9 s) while publication ran at about 19 per 10 s against 32 arrivals. Slow consumer handler time is the likely cause. Why the handler was slow is not shown.

findings.claim: Publications lagged arrivals for most of the window, building a backlog of up to 125 pending and a 38.9 s undelivered age, then drained at the end.
findings.reason: Arrivals were 32 per 10 s throughout. Publications were about 16-20 per 10 s mid-window, then 77/80/62 in the last buckets. Pending peaked at 125.

findings.claim: Consumer handler time (p95 410 ms) accounts for the slow deliveries. Auth takes about 70 ms and LedgerCore overhead is about 1 ms.
findings.reason: Handler p95 is 410 ms against a p50 of 0.024 ms. All 478 attempts succeeded, and the logged durations rise from about 75 ms to about 480 ms.

findings.claim: The delay is not caused by the API, database, connection pool or delivery failures.
findings.reason: Transfers p99 is 0.25 s with no 500s. The pool had 0 pending and 0 timeouts. There were no DB blockers, no failed deliveries and no retries.

limitations: Handler time was measured by the fixture consumer. The reason for the 410 ms handler delay is not visible.
Only the earliest 100 of 478 delivery logs are listed, and the pending gauge is sampled, so the exact slowdown onset is approximate.
next_checks: Inspect consumer handler logic and dependencies around 11:22:50-11:24:10 to see what added about 410 ms.
Check the outbox poller's delivery concurrency and run a load test against a consumer with constant latency.

alternatives.reason: At about 480 ms per delivery, sequential sending gives about 2 per s, below the 3.2 per s arrival rate. Poller concurrency was not observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox poller capacity (batch 20, 1 s interval, sequential delivery) limits throughput once per-delivery latency rises.

alternatives.reason: The catch-up burst at the end suggests the slowdown ended. The consumer's internals were not observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: The consumer slowness was a transient fixture or consumer-side condition that later cleared.

report.summary: Outbox publications lagged arrivals for about 2 minutes, building a backlog of up to 125 and an age of 39 s. The slow phase coincides with a consumer handler delay of about 410 ms, then drained. Root cause of the handler delay is not shown.

findings.claim: An outbox backlog built while transfers were committed at a steady rate, so notifications were delayed up to about 39 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals were 32 per 10 s bucket while publications were 16-20 per bucket; pending peaked at 125 and oldest age at 38.9 s, then drained.

findings.claim: The slow deliveries were slow in the consumer handler (about 410 ms), not in auth, LedgerCore, or the network.
findings.reason: The handler p95 was 410 ms against a p50 of 0.024 ms, and unattributed time was under 5 ms. All 478 attempts succeeded first try with no errors.

findings.claim: Reduced publish throughput came from slower per-delivery time with serial polling (1 s interval, batch 20), not failures or retries.
findings.reason: Zero failed deliveries; the deliveries slowed from about 75 ms to about 480 ms, and the later publication catch-up bursts (77-80 per bucket) are consistent with recovery.

alternatives.hypothesis: Database pool exhaustion or lock contention slowed outbox publishing.
alternatives.reason: Pool pending was 0, with no acquisition timeouts and no blocking sessions sampled.

alternatives.hypothesis: The transfer API was slow or erroring.
alternatives.reason: All 479 requests returned 201, with p99 at 0.25 s.

limitations: The consumer is a test fixture, so its handler delay may not reflect a real consumer. The reason for the delay is unknown.
Only the earliest 100 of 478 delivery log rows are listed, and pending is a gauge sampled every 5 s.
next_checks: Inspect the consumer handler for the cause of the roughly 410 ms delay that began around 11:22:50.
Confirm whether delivery concurrency or batch settings can absorb a slow consumer; the dirty revision may be relevant.
